The '''2024 Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council election''' was held on Thursday 2 May 2024, alongside the [[2024 United Kingdom local elections|other local elections in the United Kingdom]] being held on the same day. All 38 members of [[Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council]] in [[Warwickshire]] were elected following boundary changes.

Labour gained overall control of the council from the Conservatives, winning just enough seats to have a majority.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-03 |title=Labour gains control of Nuneaton and Bedworth council after Conservative loss |url=https://www.channel4.com/news/labour-gains-control-of-nuneaton-and-bedworth-council-after-conservative-loss |access-date=2024-05-04 |website=Channel 4 News |language=en-GB}}</ref> The Labour group leader, Chris Watkins, was formally appointed as leader of the council at the subsequent annual council meeting on 15 May 2024.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Harrison |first1=Claire |title='Be courteous' says new council leader after toxic Town Hall claims |url=https://www.coventrytelegraph.net/news/local-news/be-courteous-says-new-council-29180607 |access-date=23 July 2024 |work=Coventry Live |date=16 May 2024}}</ref>

==Background==
Nuneaton and Bedworth was a traditionally [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] council. From its creation up to [[2008 Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council election|2008]], the party held a majority on the council.<ref>{{cite web |title=Nuneaton & Bedworth Borough Council Election Results 1973-2012 |url=http://www.electionscentre.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/Nuneaton-Bedworth-1973-2012.pdf |website=Elections Centre |access-date=6 March 2024}}</ref> The [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservatives]] took control in 2008, but the council fell into [[no overall control]] in [[2010 Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council election|2010]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Nuneaton & Bedworth Vote 2010 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/shared/election2010/council/html/3728.stm |access-date=6 March 2024 |work=BBC News}}</ref> and was retaken by Labour in [[2012 Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council election|2012]].<ref>{{cite news |title=BBC News - Vote 2012 - Nuneaton & Bedworth |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/special/vote2012/council/E07000219.stm |access-date=6 March 2024 |work=BBC News}}</ref>

Labour controlled the council until [[2018 Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council election|2018]], when it again fell into no overall control. The Conservatives gained the council in [[2021 Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council election|2021]], and retained control in [[2022 Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council election|2022]]. In that election, the Conservatives gained 1 seat with 50.5% of the vote, Labour lost 2 with 34.7%, and the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] gained 1 with 14.0%.

[[File:Weddington polling station 2024 local elections.jpg|thumb|right|390px|A church hall being used as a [[polling station]] in [[Weddington, Warwickshire|Weddington]].]]

==Boundary changes==
Nuneaton and Bedworth usually elects its councillors in halves, on a 4-year cycle. However, following boundary changes, all councillors will be elected to the new wards.<ref>{{Cite legislation UK |type=si |year=2024 |number=3 |si= The Nuneaton & Bedworth (Electoral Changes) Order 2024 |accessdate=6 March 2024 }}</ref> All wards have 2 councillors. The change increases the number of councillors by 4.
